summary: Preinstall alternate-runtime dropper executes obfuscated payload via fetched Bun
details: package.json declares scripts.preinstall = 'node setup.mjs'. setup.mjs downloads the Bun runtime binary from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases (v1.3.13) into a temp directory, marks it executable, and then invokes it against a sibling file math_init.js (execFileSync(bunPath, [math_init.js])). math_init.js is a 727KB Bun-compiled bundle with heavily obfuscated identifiers (_0x-style names, a ~1000-entry mixed number/string lookup array, and a shift-based string decoder function), no readable code paths, and no reference from package.json main/typings/files/exports — the only code that references it is the preinstall setup.mjs. This is the alternate-runtime-dropper pattern: on npm install, an obfuscated payload is executed under a freshly fetched second language runtime, bypassing scanners that only inspect Node-resolved code. The undeclared executable blob plus a newly added preinstall hook in an otherwise normal React email-components library is inconsistent with the legitimate @servicetitan package contents and indicates a compromised-maintainer or namespace-hijack publish.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
